== Course of events ==

Having passed through the ordeal of shrinking to an impossibly small size, Alice finds herself in conversation with the Mouse. In her discourse, she mentions cats—a topic which, she has not yet grasped, holds particular dread for her companion.

The Mouse becomes greatly distressed at this mention. His reaction is immediate and profound, revealing in its intensity something that Alice could not have foreseen: his family harbors a hatred of cats, a sentiment so strong that mere mention of them causes him considerable upset.

In this moment, Alice's inadvertent reference has illuminated a deep family animosity, one that clearly weighs heavily upon the Mouse and speaks to grievances that run through his entire household.
